definition: Codex CLI is an open-source artificial intelligence coding agent developed by OpenAI.
details: It operates through a command-line interface and can read and modify files, execute commands, and perform software development tasks on a user's local computer. Codex CLI is part of OpenAI's broader Codex software-development platform, alongside Codex extensions for integrated development environments, desktop applications, and cloud-based development.

explainer.lead: Codex CLI is an open-source AI coding agent from OpenAI that works in a terminal. It can help with software development on your own computer by reading and changing files, running commands, and carrying out coding tasks.

tiers.eli5: It is like a coding helper sitting at your computer's text-based control panel. You can ask it to look through a project, change some code, and run commands to help finish a programming job.
tiers.practitioner: Use Codex CLI from a command-line interface for local development tasks involving project files and commands. It sits alongside Codex's IDE extensions, desktop applications, and cloud-based development options. Because it can modify files and execute commands, its actions affect the local development environment.
tiers.paperLevel: Codex CLI can be described as a local coding agent: user request -> file reads and modifications + command execution -> software-development task. It is an open-source OpenAI tool within the broader Codex platform. Its interfaces include the command line, while other Codex forms cover IDEs, desktop applications, and cloud development.

explainer.example: A developer asks Codex CLI to fix a failing program. It reads the project's files, changes the relevant code, and runs a test command to carry out the repair locally.

usedIn.name: Local software development
usedIn.detail: Reads and modifies project files and executes commands on a user's computer.

usedIn.name: Codex IDE extensions
usedIn.detail: A related part of the Codex platform for development inside integrated development environments.

usedIn.name: Desktop and cloud development
usedIn.detail: Other parts of the Codex platform support desktop applications and cloud-based development.

explainer.intuition: Instead of only suggesting code in a chat, Codex CLI works through the terminal with the files and commands used in a local software project. This lets a coding request lead directly to development actions on the user's computer.
howItWorks: A user gives the agent a software-development task through the command line.
It reads relevant files on the local computer.
It modifies files as needed for the task.
It executes commands as part of the development work.
The resulting changes and command outcomes belong to the local project.
explainer.whyItMatters: Codex CLI connects an AI coding agent directly to everyday local development work rather than limiting it to writing suggestions. Its place in the wider Codex platform also gives developers related options for IDEs, desktops, and the cloud.
misconceptions: It is not just a command-line chat tool: it can read and modify files and execute commands.
It is not the entire Codex platform: IDE extensions, desktop applications, and cloud development are separate parts.
It is not limited to cloud development: the CLI operates on a user's local computer.
